notes: Launch-day hardening against mass reporting and bot floods. Every value can be overridden at runtime with the store policy of the same key.

own_posts.notes: 2026-10-24: 6 checks per 600 s is 864 reads a day against ~2,400 publications a day, so most of our posts were never read back (own_post_checks held 3,400 rows, none hidden, while 19 accounts were suspended for hidden posts). 40 per 120 s was 28,800 reads a day, until 2026-10-24 measurements showed a hidden post stays readable through the API (4,751 posts over 48 h, none missing; 24 posts of three suspended accounts, all 200; listings match publications), so the check only catches deletion. Back to 8 per 120 s (5,760 reads a day, 0.27% of the read quota) keeps that detection and gives the quota back to the feed and comment crawlers. Posts younger than fresh_seconds still come first so a deletion is noticed within minutes.

like_pacing.notes: per_day 150 -> 400 (operator 2026-10-20): every account hit 150 by mid-afternoon, leaving pushed posts without likes. The hourly cap keeps likes spread out.

warmup.notes: 2026-10-27: new accounts are throttled for their first 36 h after the first post (2 posts/replies per hour, 15 min apart) instead of the normal 4/h and 5 min. Ban latency measured that day: no account was ever suspended within 37.3 h of its first post (median 167.7 h), so this is precaution against being reported early, not a measured effect. Set hours to 0 to switch it off.
